findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1 confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` treats the audit endpoint's `datetime` ordering field as a number, so an authorized optimized request with audit rows fails with TypeError while numeric cursor values also omit DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion required by subsequent database lookups.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — [P2 confidence 100] `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)` uses Redis's default SUM aggregation, so replaying a child whose payload already resides in its redirected segment doubles its end-timestamp score and causes later `zpopmin` eviction to retain replayed old spans over newer spans.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449 — [P2 confidence 100] `payloads[key].extend(span for span, _ in zscan_values)` removes the only enforcement of the still-accepted `max_segment_spans` constructor argument, so callers configuring a limit below 1000 receive segments exceeding their requested bound because the replacement Lua cap is hardcoded to 1000.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:845 — [advisory P3 confidence 100] `def get_result(self, limit=100, cursor=None, count_hits=False, known_hits=None, max_hits=None):` duplicates BasePaginator's query, counting, cursor-building and filtering algorithm, making future pagination fixes require two synchronized edits; the strongest argument is specialized negative-offset handling, but extracting the slice policy eliminates the duplicate get_result body while preserving that variation.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — [P2 confidence=75 advisory] `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` evicts the segment root when 1000 children finish later than it, leaving downstream consumers a segment with no `is_segment` span despite the retained root-present flag; the strongest rebuttal is that roots normally finish last, but asynchronous children and equal end timestamps defeat that assumption, so insertion eviction needs an explicit root-retention policy.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — [P1, confidence 100] Replacing SADD with `p.zadd(` while retaining `set_key = f"span-buf:s:{{{project_and_trace}}}:{parent_span_id}"` changes existing Redis keys from sets to sorted sets without conversion, versioning, or dual-format reads, so deployment rejects writes and `p.zscan(key, cursor=cursor, count=self.segment_page_size)` rejects flushes for pre-deploy buffers with WRONGTYPE, and rollback likewise cannot read newly written sorted sets.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1, confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` raises TypeError on the audit entry's datetime when an administrator requests a nonempty optimized audit-log page, returning HTTP 500 instead of audit rows.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — [P2, confidence 100] `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes a negative start directly to Django when advanced pagination receives cursor `0:-1:0`, raising an uncaught negative-indexing error and returning HTTP 500 instead of rejecting the invalid cursor with HTTP 400.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — [advisory P2, confidence 100] `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` discards spans without reporting the eviction count when a segment exceeds 1000 entries, leaving ingestion operators unable to observe truncation after this diff removes the previous span-count-exceeded metric; deliberate bounded retention justifies eviction but does not justify eliminating its loss signal.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — [P1, confidence 100] `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` adds an unrelated audit-log API mode and shared-paginator behavior changes to a task whose stated scope is spans-buffer insertion eviction, shipping a separate externally selectable pagination feature to audit-log users without any requirement connecting it to span buffering.

tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:126 — [P2 confidence=100 advisory] The updated fixtures use `end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0,` for every span and contain at most five spans per case, so deleting `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)` or reversing its eviction order leaves their assertions unchanged while oversized production traces lose the insertion-cap or retain the wrong spans; the strongest rebuttal is that permutation tests exercise real Redis merges, but those merges never cross 1000 entries or compare distinct timestamps, leaving the new eviction behavior unverified.

goldens.comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — [P2, confidence 100] `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes a negative start directly to Django when advanced pagination receives cursor `0:-1:0`, raising an uncaught negative-indexing error and returning HTTP 500 instead of rejecting the invalid cursor with HTTP 400.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment. Both point out that in OptimizedCursorPaginator's get_result() method, when there's a negative cursor offset, the code passes this negative value directly to Django queryset slicing (start_offset), which causes an error. The candidate provides more specific details about the consequences (HTTP 500 instead of 400) and gives a concrete example (cursor 0:-1:0), but it's fundamentally the same issue about negative offset handling in the advanced features branch.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment. Both point out that negative offset values can be passed to queryset slicing. The golden comment explains the root cause (in BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, start_offset = offset is set without clamping, allowing negative values). The candidate issue describes the consequence of this same bug (negative start passed to Django queryset slicing, causing an error). They're describing the same bug - the lack of clamping/validation of negative offset values in pagination.
